title: The Fourier–Deligne transform
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a prime invertible in $\Lambda$, and let $\pi:V\to S$ and $\pi':V'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Put $W=V\times_SV'$, with projections $p_1:W\to V$ and $p_2:W\to V'$. Assume $p=0$ in $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, and fix $b\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ and an additive character $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to\Lambda^\times$. Let $\mathcal K_\psi=\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}$ be the Fourier kernel of [def-fd-kernel] (with the data and general coefficient convention of its current blueprint statement).

Use the unbounded derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Regard $\mathcal K_\psi$ as the complex $\mathcal K_\psi[0]$ concentrated in degree zero. The pullback $p_1^*$ means the functor on these derived categories induced by termwise inverse image of module sheaves: the inverse image identifies the constant ring sheaves and is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so it descends by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The symbol $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ means the derived tensor product of [def-kun-derived-tensor].

Assume $p_2$ admits a compactification [def-nagata-compactification], and choose one, written $c=(j,q)$ with $W\xrightarrow{j}\overline W\xrightarrow{q}V'$, $j$ an open immersion, $q$ proper, and $qj=p_2$. Here compactification has the current blueprint meaning: the open immersion need not be quasi-compact. Write
$$
 Rp_{2,!}=Rq_*\circ D(j_!):D(W_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(V'_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)
$$
for the functor computed using this chosen compactification. Here $j_!$ is etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]; its termwise application preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and $D(j_!)$ is the induced functor of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The functor $Rq_*$ is the unbounded total right derived functor of the sheaf direct image $q_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], constructed by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] using the K-injective resolutions of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], which exist for these module-sheaf categories by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Thus it is the total derived functor of $Qq_*$ on the homotopy category; this functor is exact because termwise application of the additive functor $q_*$ respects shifts and cone differentials. For a complex $L$ on $W$, it sends $QL$ to $Qq_*I$ after a K-injective resolution $j_!L\to I$ on $\overline W$.

For $r\in\mathbf Z$, the *Fourier–Deligne transform* is the composite functor
$$
 \operatorname{FT}_\psi:D(V_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(V'_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda),\qquad
 \operatorname{FT}_\psi(K):=Rp_{2,!}\bigl(p_1^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda\mathcal K_\psi[0]\bigr)[r].
$$
Its value on a morphism $a:K\to L$ is $\bigl(Rp_{2,!}(p_1^*a\otimes^L\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal K_\psi[0]})\bigr)[r]$. The cohomological shift has $(C[r])^i=C^{i+r}$ and differential $(-1)^r d_C^{i+r}$, and shifts morphisms degreewise (the cochain shift of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], which induces the shift $[1]$ of the triangulated category $D(V'_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)$ and its integer powers $[r]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]). In the vector-bundle application of [def-fd-kernel], $V=V_0\to S_0$ has rank $r$, $V'=V_0^\vee$ is its dual, and $b$ is evaluation; the shift by the rank is Laumon's normalization. On the affine line $r=1$. The transform $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ is the same construction, using $\Psi^{-1}$ in place of $\Psi$.

This defines the composite for the chosen compactification; comparison with another compactification and preservation of bounded constructible objects are separate properties.

proof.text: Prove the coefficient-prime and base-characteristic obligations using Mathlib charP_of_card_eq_prime_pow and the recorded equality #k0=p^a. The distinct prime l has nonzero image in k0 by CharP.cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime, so its image in each model residue field under the structure map is a unit. No finite-type assumption on the model is used for this unit assertion.

For fourierModelProjection_frobenius, specialize galoisMap_projections of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] to the inverse q-power automorphism. Its first projection equation is exactly the required equality of scheme morphisms. This supplies the equality used in the already constructed descent Weil structure.

For fourierTensorFrobenius_naturality, take the common-stage natural isomorphism in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], whose components equal canonicalCommonStagePullbackTensor. Apply naturality to (f,id_N). Postcompose with tensor(id,N.str), reassociate, and use functoriality of tensor. The two product arrows coincide componentwise by the identity and composition laws. This proves naturality of the specified components, rather than choosing different components.

The affine-model finite-type, quasi-compact and separated assertions follow from the existing affine-space instances. Base change and composition give the product structure morphism finite type and quasi-compact. Its source is locally Noetherian over the finite field and compact over the compact spectrum, hence Noetherian. For the characteristic of its global sections, the pair of zero sections gives a section Spec(k0) -> W, so the global-section ring is nontrivial. Apply CharP.of_ringHom_of_ne_zero to k0 -> Gamma(W,O_W). The zero-section argument also covers the empty coordinate type, and the characteristic assertion requires no finiteness assumption on that type.

lean.note: §1(B): the prior WeilFourierTransform interface accepts the derived category of Weil sheaves, whereas def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex and sk-def-trace now require IsoAlgebra fixed pairs in the intrinsic adic common-stage derived category. This module publicly retains the full existing ordinary-etale functor and the previous general Weil-pairing/affine interfaces, and adds the actual fixed-pair functor on objects and all morphisms using the recorded adic character kernel, normalized geometric-fibre pullback, monoidal Frobenius comparison and adjunction-mate compact support. The signed shift is formed on the kernel over the finite-field model before descent: the canonical tensor/shift and compact-support/shift comparisons identify this with Rp2!(p1*K tensor kernel)[r]. No arbitrary Frobenius isomorphism, arbitrary kernel, equivalence with derived Weil sheaves, or trace-formula hypothesis is chosen. Tensor naturality is a named postponed obligation; functoriality is inherited from the existing pullback, tensor and compact-support functors. The affine specialization supplies the standard pairing and r=card n, including rank one.

blueprint_update.statement:

character $\Psi$ and the Fourier kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ on

$p_1:V\times_SV'\to V$ and $p_2:V\times_SV'\to V'$ be the projections,
and assume that $p_2$ admits a compactification, so that the
compact-support direct image $Rp_{2,!}$ is defined. For $r\in\mathbf Z$,
the *Fourier–Deligne transform* is the functor

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi:D(V_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)\longrightarrow
D(V'_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda),\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K):=Rp_{2,!}\bigl(p_1^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)[r],
$$

between the derived categories of étale sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules,
where $\mathcal K_\psi$ is regarded as a complex concentrated in degree $0$
and $p_1^*$ is the derived pullback. In the application of
[def-fd-kernel], $V_0\to S_0$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$,
$V'=V_0^\vee$, and the shift $[r]$ by the relative dimension is Laumon's
normalization. The transform $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ is the same
construction with $\Psi^{-1}$ in place of $\Psi$.
